newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Court allows Malaysian tycoon to contest party post.
newsitem.headline: Court allows Malaysian tycoon to contest party post.

text.p: The High Court has allowed tycoon Joseph Chong to contest the presidentship of Malaysia's Gerakan party, two days after he was sacked from its membership, the Bernama news agency said on Saturday.

The court granted Chong, a member of parliament and head of industrial group Westmont Holdings, an injunction to prevent the Gerakan party from disqualifying him from contesting the party elections on October 5.
The Gerakan party sacked Chong from its central committee on September 26, after he decided to challenge the incumbent and Primary Industries Minister Lim Keng Yaik for the party's top job.
Chong submitted his nomination papers to challenge Lim for the top post last Thursday, just hours before he was expelled as the party's central committee member.

Chong is managing director of Wing Tiek Holdings Bhd, which has a controlling stake in National Steel Corp of the Philippines. He also controls property-based Westmont Land (Asia) Bhd and engineering concern Westmont Industries Bhd.
Chong could not be reached for a comment.
The Gerakan party controls northern Penang state, known as Malaysia's Silicon Valley because of the many big electronics firms located on the island.
The mostly Chinese party is also one of several race-based groups that make up Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's multi-racial National Front.
